subject.title: feat: sleep tool — pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` tool, and if so should it be implemented as a dedicated gateway resume primitive or as a cron-backed `agentTurn` targeted at the caller session with explicit sandbox policy?
rationale: This PR changes the model-facing core tool surface and crosses gateway cron, session-state, interruption, restart, and sandbox boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent API and security semantics safely.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
options.body: Accept the feature direction but require a revised implementation that uses a supported caller-session wake path, proves interruption/restart behavior, and keeps sandbox exposure explicit.

options.title: Keep existing cron/session guidance
options.body: Reject a new core tool for now and leave delayed work to cron, process completion wakes, and `sessions_yield` where they already have ownership.

options.title: Narrow to an extension seam
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime extension point instead of adding a default built-in tool if optional scheduling should live outside core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction but require a revised implementation that uses a supported caller-session wake path, proves interruption/restart behavior, and keeps sandbox exposure explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron and agent-runtime history plus the prior canonical issue review make this the strongest product/API routing owner among the observed candidates.
